transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate it. 

Um, well... I guess I'm here because, well, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but people have been saying my talking gets a bit mixed up sometimes. It's nothing too terrible, I don't think, and it's not on purpose, I promise. But... like, I'll try to explain something simple, maybe about the keys for the building I clean, and then somehow I'm talking about the jail, and then the prayer rug, and then chess pieces. 

I just... I guess I jump around a bit, and folks tell me they just cannot follow what I'm saying. I try really hard to make sense, I do. I'm really trying to be clear for you right now. Am I making sense so far, doctor? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or overly happy lately?

Well, um... I guess I do have days where I feel just... really, really good. Maybe a bit more than just regular happy? Like, I feel so strong and... well, powerful, I guess you could say. I get to laughing and talking real loud with everybody at work, just feeling on top of the world. 

But... um, I hate to admit this next part, doctor, because I really try to get along with everyone. But sometimes, when I'm feeling like that... if somebody questions me or gets in my way, I... I can get a little testy. I might snap at them or shout over something real small. I always feel terrible about it right after, I promise. I don't mean to be rude to folks, it just sort of comes out before I can catch it. 

Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound like an awful person... I'm just trying to answer you as honest as I can. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
When you’re feeling especially strong or on top of the world, do you need less sleep than usual?

Oh, um... well, yes sir. I suppose I do. But it's actually... well, I hope it's alright to say, it's actually real helpful for my job. I don't want you to think I'm doing anything unhealthy, I promise. 

But when I'm feeling that good, I... I really don't need much rest at all. I can lay down for maybe two or three hours, and then I'm up way before the sun even comes out. And I feel just fine! Really fresh, actually. I'll start planning out all my mopping and buffing for the day, and it just feels like... like sleep is something other people need, but not me. I get so much done for the building when I'm like that. 

Is... is it a bad thing to sleep less if I'm still doing a real good job at work? I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing. I hope I'm answering your questions the way you need me to, doctor.
Have you ever heard voices when you were not feeling especially up or unusually good?

Oh... um. Well, I really want to be completely honest with you, doctor, because I know you need the whole picture to help me. It's just... a little hard to admit this next part. I really don't want you to think poorly of me, or think I'm... well, you know, crazy or anything like that. 

But... yes sir. Even when I'm just having a regular, calm week... you know, not feeling all powerful and high up, but not feeling down in the dumps either... I still... well, there was a stretch of time, definitely for more than two weeks, where I was still experiencing some strange things. 

Like, um... I would hear a man's voice up in the air vents at the building. Just talking. And... I also got to believing that the folks working in the offices were making little signals to each other about me when I walked by. I tried real hard not to let it bother my work, I promise! I just kept my head down and kept my mop moving, trying to be a good employee. 

I hope it's okay that I'm telling you this... I know it sounds a bit odd, but I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. Am I doing okay explaining it?
During that stretch when you heard the voice and felt people were signaling about you, were you having those experiences while your mood was completely normal?

Yes, sir. That's... well, that's exactly right. I hope I didn't make it sound too confusing before. 

But yes, there were definitely times—calmer weeks, you know? When I wasn't feeling all revved up and powerful, and I wasn't feeling completely down and hopeless either. Just... just my normal, regular self, going in to do my shift. And even then, for a good stretch... definitely more than two weeks, I'd say... I was still hearing that man's voice up in the vents. And I still had that strong feeling about the office folks making those little hand signals about me when I'd come through with the trash cart.

I really tried to just focus on doing a good job with the cleaning and not let it show. I didn't want anyone thinking I couldn't handle my work, you know? But it was happening even when my mood felt just fine. 

Is... is that the kind of detail you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you're looking for so you can help me. I hope I'm being helpful.
